gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: Some metals are magnetic; ___ are not.
gaps.explanation: 'Some ... others ...' contrasts unspecified groups; 'the others' would need a closed, known set.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was ___ attended than the organisers had hoped.
gaps.explanation: 'Well attended' compares with the adverb: less well attended.

gaps.sentence: It took a great ___ of courage to admit the mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of courage' is the standard pattern with uncountables; 'a great number of' needs countables.

gaps.sentence: Some people like classical music, while ___ prefer jazz.
gaps.explanation: The pattern 'some ... others ...' contrasts unspecified groups; 'the others' would need a previously defined group.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ luggage that the taxi couldn't take it all.
gaps.explanation: 'So much luggage that …' — luggage is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.
